title: You didn’t expect God to call you like that.
paragraphs: You didn’t expect God to call you like that.
Not in the middle of something ordinary. Not when you’re young, unnoticed, still figuring life out. You assumed—if God ever spoke—it would be loud, undeniable, reserved for the “spiritual elite.”
But the story of Samuel dismantles that assumption completely.
It begins quietly in 1 Samuel. A child. A temple. A fading priesthood. And a God who refuses to stay silent.

Samuel wasn’t a prophet yet. He wasn’t known, respected, or influential. He was just a boy serving under Eli—a priest whose own spiritual sensitivity had dulled over time. The environment Samuel grew up in was religious… but not necessarily alive.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because you can be surrounded by “church things” and still not recognize God’s voice.
Scripture says:
“The word of the Lord was rare in those days; there was no frequent vision.” (1 Samuel 3:1)
Let that sit.
God wasn’t absent—but people had stopped hearing Him.
And then one night, everything shifted.
Samuel was lying down, probably exhausted from routine service. Nothing dramatic. No buildup. No warning.
Then it happened.
“Samuel!”
He woke up immediately. Ran to Eli.
“Here I am, for you called me.”
But Eli hadn’t called him.
This happened again.
And again.
Three times Samuel heard a voice—and three times he misidentified it.
That’s the part people skip too quickly.
Samuel was hearing God… but he didn’t know it was God.
And that’s where you are right now.

You’ve felt conviction and called it anxiety.
You’ve sensed a pull and labeled it coincidence.
You’ve heard truth echo in your spirit—and dismissed it as your own thoughts.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God’s voice doesn’t always arrive with thunder. Sometimes it sounds like a whisper you almost ignore.
And you keep running to the wrong explanations.
You knew.
God saw it.
By the third time, something finally clicked for Eli. Even in his spiritual dullness, he recognized what was happening.
He told Samuel:
“Go, lie down, and if He calls you, you shall say, ‘Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears.’”
That response changed everything.
Because this moment wasn’t just about hearing.
It was about surrender.
Samuel went back. Laid down again. Heart probably racing now.
Then God came.
Not from a distance.
Not vaguely.
“The Lord came and stood, calling as at other times, ‘Samuel! Samuel!’”
Read that again.
God didn’t shout from heaven.
He came close.
And this time, Samuel answered differently:
“Speak, for Your servant hears.”
That’s the turning point.
Not when God spoke.
But when Samuel was ready to listen.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
And what God said next wasn’t soft.
It wasn’t comforting.
It was judgment.
God revealed the coming downfall of Eli’s house because of unrepentant sin—sin Eli knew about, sin he tolerated, sin he refused to confront.
This is where most modern narratives would soften things.
But Scripture doesn’t.
God’s first recorded words to Samuel were heavy, holy, and terrifying.
Because the call of God isn’t just about purpose.
It’s about truth.
And truth exposes.
Samuel had to carry a message that cost him comfort. He had to speak what others avoided. And when morning came, he was afraid to tell Eli.
Of course he was.
Truth will always test your obedience.
But he spoke it anyway.
And from that moment on, everything changed.
“Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.” (1 Samuel 3:19)
That’s not just a calling story.
That’s a transformation story.
A boy who didn’t recognize God’s voice became a man who carried God’s word with authority.
But don’t miss how it started.
It started with confusion.
It moved through misinterpretation.
It required correction.
And it culminated in surrender.
That’s the path you’ve been resisting.
You keep waiting for clarity before obedience.
God is waiting for surrender before clarity.
Two different directions.
Only one leads to life.
Because the deeper reality behind Samuel’s story isn’t just about hearing God’s voice—it’s about why we struggle to hear Him at all.
Sin dulls perception.
Distraction numbs awareness.
Pride resists correction.
And familiarity with religion can blind you to real relationship.
But then comes Jesus.
Because what Samuel experienced in fragments, Jesus Christ fulfills completely.
“In the beginning was the Word…” (John 1:1)
God didn’t just speak anymore.
He became the message.
Through Christ, the distance between God and man was closed—not by effort, but by grace.
Because the truth is, you don’t just need to hear God.
You need to be reconciled to Him.
Sin separated you.
Not your mistakes alone—but your nature.
And no amount of “trying harder” fixes that.
That’s why Jesus came.
“To seek and to save the lost.” (Luke 19:10)

He lived the life you couldn’t live.
Died the death your sin deserved.
And rose again so you could actually hear God—not in fear, but in relationship.
But here’s where it gets real again.
You can hear this… and still walk away unchanged.
Just like Eli heard warnings and didn’t act.
So now the moment is yours.
Not dramatic.
Not forced.
But real.
You’ve heard something in this.
You felt it.
That quiet tension.
That nudge.
That discomfort you can’t explain.
That’s not random.
If your response is still “I don’t know if that’s God”… you’re standing exactly where Samuel stood the third time.
And now you know what to say.
Not perfectly.
Not eloquently.
Just honestly:
Speak, Lord.
Because I’ve been hearing… and I haven’t been listening.
If that hit you, don’t bury it.
Say it. Even here. Even simply.
And don’t keep this to yourself—someone close to you is ignoring the same voice you’ve been hearing. Send this to them. Let it interrupt them the way this just interrupted you.
You’ll need to come back to it—because the voice of God doesn’t stop after one call.
And if you’re ready to go deeper, not just inspired but discipled—there’s a path for that:
Because hearing God is one thing.
Belonging to Him is everything.
